subject.title: Onboarding Wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup as a mandatory step

question: Should first-run onboarding and `openclaw configure` make memory embedding setup mandatory, prominently optional, or diagnostic-only, and what credential/probe UX should it use?
rationale: The missing setup surface is source-proven, but the requested mandatory behavior affects first-run completion, provider cost, credential storage, daemon environment behavior, local/FTS-only workflows, and security posture.

options.title: Prominent Optional Setup
options.body: Add a visible skippable memory setup/readiness path that configures the existing provider/model and SecretRef or API-key fields, then verifies with a probe or memory status guidance.

options.title: Mandatory Memory Gate
options.body: Require users to configure embeddings or explicitly choose FTS-only before onboarding completes, improving recall readiness at the cost of first-run friction.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep onboarding lean and rely on doctor, status, and memory CLI guidance, accepting that some users may miss memory readiness until later.

recommendation.title: Prominent Optional Setup
recommendation.body: Add a visible skippable memory setup/readiness path that configures the existing provider/model and SecretRef or API-key fields, then verifies with a probe or memory status guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman is the current assignee and participated in the product-scope discussion on this exact report.
